 Hells Gate Gorge to Remain Closed Throughout El Niño Rainy Season Over Flood Risks 
 -->
 --> 
 by Maxwell Amunga on Monday, 9 November 2026 - 6:21 pm 
 An image of elephants in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, with a tour car with tourists, and a KWS logo on the side. 
 Photo 
 Matador Network 
 -->
 The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) has announced the closure of Hells Gate Gorge in Naivasha throughout the El Niño rainy season.
 The announcement, made on Monday, November 9, will restrict tourists and other visitors from accessing the popular attraction as heavy rainfall increases the risk of deadly flash floods.
 The closure comes as anticipated El Niño rains, which will extend up to early next year according to the Kenya Meteorological Service Authority (KMSA), threaten several parts of the country, raising concerns about sudden flooding that could trap unsuspecting visitors.
 Visitors will therefore have to avoid the gorge throughout the rainy season, even when conditions inside the national park appear safe.
 A section of the Ol Njorowa gorge in Naivasha 
 TripAdvisor 
 Flash floods at Hells Gate can occur even when there is no rainfall within the national park itself.
 Heavy downpours in surrounding highland areas, including Mount Longonot, Mai Mahiu, Nairobi, Kedong and Suswa, send large volumes of water downstream.
 The runoff flows through natural drainage channels into the narrow Ol Njorowa Gorge, where water levels can rise within minutes.
 The gorge's steep rock walls and narrow passages leave visitors with little room to escape when powerful floodwaters suddenly sweep through. 
 In September 2019, seven people died after flash floods swept away a group of 13 visitors exploring the gorge.
 The victims included five Kenyan tourists, a local tour guide and one foreign visitor, with rescue teams recovering bodies downstream.
 Another tragedy occurred in 2012 when seven youths from PCEA Mukarara Church in Dagoretti died during an excursion inside the gorge.
 KWS says the precautionary measure is intended to protect visitors following previous incidents in which people lost their lives inside the gorge during rainy seasons. 
“ Sometimes it does not rain in Hells Gate National Park, but it has rained upstream, which drains water to the gorge. So, we always make sure that if it is raining, we take the necessary precautions to prevent loss of life,” KWS stated. 
 Kenya Wildlife Services Director General Erustus Kanga.
